program.title: Tennis All-Court Player: Shoulder-Safe Strength & Rotational Power Foundation

athlete_analysis.profile_summary: Intermediate tennis all-court player training 1x/week for 60 min. Mild shoulder soreness after serving. Requires shoulder-friendly pressing, rotational power, deceleration capacity, and sport-specific trunk control.
primary_constraints: Mild shoulder soreness post-serve; avoid high-overhead or aggressive pressing until pain-free
Single training day/week limits volume; must prioritize transfer over isolation
Equipment limited to dumbbells, bands, court, medicine ball; no barbell or machine access
sport_demands: Rotational power and deceleration for groundstrokes, serves, and lateral movement
Shoulder/scapular durability for serve, volley, and overhead; elbow/wrist stability
Trunk anti-rotation and hip control for directional shot change and recovery
athlete_analysis.block_priority: Build rotational strength, scapular stability, and deceleration capacity while managing shoulder load. Single session must deliver pressing, pulling, core anti-rotation, and lower-body unilateral work.

weeks.theme: Shoulder-friendly horizontal press, unilateral pull, anti-rotation core, and single-leg stability.

workouts.title: Pressing, Pulling, Anti-Rotation & Single-Leg Stability
adaptation_targets: Unilateral lat strength and rotational control
Anti-rotation trunk stiffness and hip control
sport_transfer: Shoulder durability for serving and volleys through scapular control
Rotational power transfer from ground through trunk to racket
Single-leg balance and deceleration for court movement and split-step
workouts.why_this_session: Develop pressing strength without overhead load stress; build rotational and anti-rotation trunk power; train single-leg stability for sport-specific directional movement and braking.

warmup.name: Dead Bug
warmup.purpose: Activate core and establish neutral spine stability before loaded work.

warmup.name: Side-Lying Dumbbell External Rotation
warmup.purpose: Activate rotator cuff and build shoulder comfort before pressing.
warmup.load_guidance: Light dumbbell (2–5 kg); focus on control, not load.

warmup.name: Open Book Thoracic Rotation
warmup.purpose: Mobilize thoracic spine and prepare trunk for rotation and pressing patterns.

main_work.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
main_work.purpose: Safe horizontal pressing pattern that eliminates shoulder stress from depth while building chest, shoulder, and triceps strength.
main_work.load_guidance: Moderate load; pain-free shoulder position mandatory. If any soreness, reduce reps to 5 and add 30 sec rest.
main_work.tempo: 2 sec down, 1 sec hold, 1 sec up

main_work.name: Single-Arm Cable Pulldown
main_work.purpose: Unilateral lat strength and scapular control; anti-rotation core demand from single-sided load.
main_work.load_guidance: Moderate load; ribs set before each pull to prevent rotation.
main_work.tempo: 1 sec down, 2 sec hold, 2 sec up

main_work.name: Half-Kneeling Pallof Press
main_work.purpose: Anti-rotation trunk stiffness and hip control; replicate lateral movement stability needed for directional court changes.
main_work.load_guidance: Band or light cable load; emphasize stacked ribs and pelvis throughout.
main_work.tempo: 2 sec press, 1 sec hold, 2 sec return

main_work.name: Single-Leg Leg Press
main_work.purpose: Unilateral lower-body strength, balance, and deceleration capacity for single-leg braking and directional movement.
main_work.load_guidance: Moderate load; stable foot placement and controlled descent without knee deviation.
main_work.tempo: 2 sec down, 1 sec hold, 1 sec up

cooldown.name: Thread The Needle
cooldown.purpose: Restore upper-back and shoulder mobility after pressing and pulling work.

cooldown.name: Wall Slide
cooldown.purpose: Reinforce scapular control and shoulder posture; reduce post-session stiffness.

injury_modifications: If shoulder soreness persists or worsens 24 h post-session, replace Dumbbell Floor Press with band-only horizontal press (3×8, RPE 4–5) or bodyweight floor press.
If knee discomfort arises in Single-Leg Leg Press, substitute Lateral Lunge (3×8 each side, bodyweight or light dumbbell).
If low-back pain appears during Pallof Press, reduce reps to 6 and shorten duration to 45 sec per side.

weeks.progression_rule: Session establishes baseline movement quality under sport load. Pain-free shoulder performance in floor press confirms readiness; if soreness occurs post-session, regress to bodyweight or band-only work next week.

program.nutrition_focus: Support recovery and shoulder durability: adequate protein (1.6–2.0 g/kg), anti-inflammatory micronutrients (omega-3, vitamin C, polyphenols), hydration (3–4 L/day). No supplement requirement unless deficiency is confirmed.
recovery_focus: Monitor 24-hour shoulder soreness response after session; stable or improved response confirms load tolerance.
Sleep 7–8 h nightly; emphasize consistent bedtime to support adaptive response.
Use low-intensity movement (walking, easy mobility) on non-training days to reduce stiffness without adding fatigue.
safety_notes: Shoulder pain is the primary constraint; all pressing and overhead work requires pain-free completion. Stop immediately if sharp pain occurs.
No max-effort tests or explosive plyometric serves until shoulder stability is confirmed over 2–3 weeks of pain-free training.
Single-leg work requires controlled tempo and neutral knee alignment; do not allow knee valgus or uncontrolled deceleration.
assumptions: Athlete has access to leg press machine; if not available, substitute Single-Leg Leg Press with Lateral Lunge (3×8 each side, RPE 6–7).
Shoulder soreness is mechanical (post-serve) and not structural; medical clearance assumed for training.
Athlete can tolerate floor-based pressing and kneeling positions without pain.
Training day is Monday; if schedule changes, apply the same protocol to the new preferred day.
